IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r9.speaker: آخر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r9.claim: Another interpreter reverses the construction to mean that the person’s love of wealth is intense.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r9.anchor: وقال آخر في قوله سبحانه: وإنه لحب الخير لشديد

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r11.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r11.claim: He rejects imposing inversion on the Qur’an without sound grounds: poets may reverse wording by mistake, for rhyme or meter, or from poetic necessity.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r11.anchor: وهذا ما لا يجوز لأحد أن يحكم به على كتاب الله عز وجل لو لم يجد له مذهبا

ITQAN:v3p103/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p103/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p103/r1.claim: In 100:8, love of good means that a person’s love of wealth is intense.

TABRISI:100:4-11/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:4-11/r10.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:100:4-11/r10.claim: Strong love of wealth makes the person miserly and withholding of God's due; al-Farraʾ instead reads that he intensely loves wealth.
TABRISI:100:4-11/r10.anchor: من أجله لبخيل شحيح يمنع منه حق الله تعالى عن الحسن

TABRISI:100:4-11/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:4-11/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:100:4-11/r11.claim: God calls wealth good because people regard it as good, just as fighting is called harm because people label it so.
TABRISI:100:4-11/r11.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: سمى الله سبحانه المال خيرا وعسى أن يكون خبيثا وحراما

QASHANI:100:6-11/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:100:6-11/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:100:6-11/r3.claim: Strong love of good means attachment to wealth or miserliness from loving it, causing hoarding and veiling; alternatively, a person is constricted even toward good leading to truth.
QASHANI:100:6-11/r3.anchor: أي: وإنه لحب المال لقوي أو لأجل حب المال بخيل، فلذلك يحتجب به

FARRA:v3p285/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p285/r3.speaker: الكلبي
FARRA:v3p285/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets شديد as miserly, and الخير as wealth.

FARRA:v3p285/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p285/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p285/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes the person strong in love of wealth; al-Farrāʾ prefers “intense in love for wealth,” with الحب omitted after being stated once and for rhyme.
FARRA:v3p285/r4.anchor: ونرى والله أعلم- أن المعنى: وإنه للخير لشديد الحب

FARRA:v3p285/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p285/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p285/r5.claim: The omitted-love construction parallels عاصف describing the wind in the preceding phrase, though the word is attached to day for rhyme.
FARRA:v3p285/r5.anchor: والعصوف لا يكون للأيام إنما يكون للريح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r3.claim: The following clauses explain this innate, variable ingratitude and show that it appears through speech, intention, conduct, or neglect.

NAHHAS:v5p278/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p278/r4.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p278/r4.claim: One interpretation takes لشديد القوى to mean strong in physical powers.
NAHHAS:v5p278/r4.anchor: في معناه أقوال قيل لشديد القوى

NAHHAS:v5p278/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p278/r5.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p278/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the human is intensely attached to wealth; the implied wording is شديد الحب, with the material after شديد omitted.
NAHHAS:v5p278/r5.anchor: وقول الفراء أن المعنى أن الإنسان للخير لشديد الحب فالتقدير عنده إنه لحب الخير لشديد الحب

NAHHAS:v5p278/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p278/r6.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v5p278/r6.claim: Ali ibn Sulayman explains the phrase as being severe because of love of wealth, that is, miserly.
NAHHAS:v5p278/r6.anchor: سمعت علي بن سليمان يقول كما تقول أن أكرم فلانا لك أي من أجلك أي وإنه من أجل حب الخير أي المال لشديد أي لبخيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r14.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r14.anchor: المال , قاله ابن عباس , ومجاهد وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r15.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r15.claim: He understands الخير as worldly life.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r16.claim: It could mean the person's intense love for what he chooses for himself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r16.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : أن الخير ها هنا الاختيار

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r17.claim: شديد may mean that his love is strong and increasing, or that he is miserly with wealth and withholds God's due, as Hasan explains.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r17.anchor: لشديد الحب للخير , وشدة الحب قوته وتزايده . الثاني : لشحيح بالمال يمنع حق الله منه

RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r1.claim: Al-khayr here means wealth, as in 2:180 and 70:21; people call money good, while God calls the wounds of war harm in 3:174.
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r1.anchor: الخير المال من قوله تعالى : { إن ترك خيرا } وقوله : { وإذا مسه الخير منوعا } وهذالأن الناس يعدون المال فيما بينهم خيرا كما أنه تعالى سمي ما ينال المجاهد من الجراح وأذى الحرب سوءا

RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r2.claim: Al-shadīd means miserly and withholding; the terms shadīda and mutashaddid describe such a person.
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r2.anchor: والشديد البخيل الممسك ، يقال : فلان شديدة ومتشدد

RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r3.speaker: طرفة
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r3.claim: Ṭarafa's verse supplies mutashaddid as a poetic example of a person fiercely withholding valuable wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r3.anchor: قال طرفة : أرى الموت يعتام الكرام ويصطفي … عقيلة مال الفاحش المتشدد

RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r4.claim: One interpretation is that love of money makes the person miserly and withholding.
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r4.anchor: أحدها : أنه لأجل حب المال لبخيل ممسك

RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r5.claim: A second interpretation takes shadīd as strong and capable: he energetically pursues and prefers worldly life but is weak in worship and gratitude.
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r5.anchor: وثانيها : أن يكون المراد من الشديدة القرى ، ويكون المعنى وإنه لحب المال وإيثار الدنيا وطلبها قوي مطيق ، وهو لحب عبادة الله وشكر نعمه ضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r6.claim: A third interpretation portrays him as constricted and withholding rather than generous and expansive in his love of wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r6.anchor: وثالثها : أراد إنه لحب الخيرات غير هني منبسط ولكنه شديد منقبض

RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r7.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the phrase as severe love of wealth, with the first mention of love standing for an omitted second one, as in 14:18.
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r7.anchor: قال الفراء : يجوز أن يكون المعنى وإنه لحب الخير لشديد الحب يعني أنه يحب المال ، ويحب كونه محبا له

RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r8.speaker: قطرب
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r8.claim: Quṭrub glosses it as loving wealth intensely, by analogy with saying that someone is a great smasher of Zayd.
RAZI-FULL:v32p64/r8.anchor: قال قطرب : أي إنه شديد حب الخير ، كقولك إنه لزيد ضروب أي أنه ضروب زيد

TABATABAI:100:6-11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r5.claim: Some read the phrase causally: because of love of wealth a person is intensely miserly; others take it to mean that a person strongly loves money and withholds God's due and charitable spending.
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r5.anchor: للتعليل والخير المال، والمعنى وإن الإنسان لأجل حب المال لشديد أي بخيل شحيح،

TABATABAI:100:6-11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r6.claim: The author allows خير to mean good generally: people naturally love good, but mistake worldly goods and ornaments for good and forget gratitude to their Lord.
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r6.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يكون المراد بالخير مطلقه ويكون المراد أن حب الخير فطري للإنسان ثم إنه يرى عرض الدنيا وزينتها خيرا

THALABI:v10p272/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p272/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p272/r1.claim: The cited verse depicts death choosing the wealth of a persistently miserly person, supporting the sense of شديد حب الخير as avarice.
THALABI:v10p272/r1.anchor: أرى الموت يعتام الكرام ويصطفي … عقيلة مال الفاحش المتشدد

THALABI:v10p272/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p272/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p272/r2.claim: الفاحش can also mean a miser; the Qurʾanic command against الفحشاء is glossed here as a command against miserliness.
THALABI:v10p272/r2.anchor: والفاحش: البخيل أيضا قال الله سبحانه: ويأمركم بالفحشاء أي البخل

THALABI:v10p272/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p272/r3.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p272/r3.claim: An alternative gloss reads the phrase as saying that he is intensely attached to wealth.
THALABI:v10p272/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه: وإنه لحب الخير لقوي

THALABI:v10p272/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p272/r4.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p272/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the syntax as an inversion of شديد الحب للخير, with شديد omitted because حب has already appeared.
THALABI:v10p272/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: كان موضع الحب أن يكون بعد شديد وأن يضاف شديد إليه

THALABI:v10p272/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p272/r5.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p272/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the inversion also suits the verse endings, as in describing a day as windy after wind was already mentioned.
THALABI:v10p272/r5.anchor: ولرؤوس الآيات كقوله سبحانه: في يوم عاصف والعصوف لا يكون للأيام

ASAD-NOTES:100:6/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:100:6/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:100:6/r2.claim: The human being is ardently devoted to wealth.
ASAD-NOTES:100:6/r2.anchor: to the love of wealth is he most ardently devoted.

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r1.claim: An ʾinsan saying delays the eschatological resolution of the enigmatic oath opening; Neuwirth calls the saying a motif that later becomes a topos.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die eschatologische Auflösung der enigmatischen Schwureinleitung wird durch einen – später zum Topos werdenden – ʾinsān-Spruch retardiert

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r2.claim: Verses 6–8 form the surah's structural center and contrast with the dynamic verbal and participial clauses around them; these are its only nominal sentences.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r2.anchor: Sprachlich stehen V. 6–8, welche die strukturelle Mitte der Sure bilden, in deutlichem Kontrast zur dynamischen Aufgewühltheit von V. 1–5 und V. 9–11

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r3.claim: The passage accuses humanity of publicly bearing witness to ingratitude toward God in verses 6–7 and of possessiveness in verse 8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r3.anchor: Inhaltlich werden dem Menschen eine öffentlich „Bezeugung“ von Undank gegen Gott (V. 6–7) sowie Besitzgier (V. 8) vorgeworfen.

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r4.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r4.claim: Neuwirth reads these failings as examples of pre-Islamic anthropocentric values.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r4.anchor: Neuwirth sieht hierin exemplarische Stellvertreter für den anthropozentrischen Wertekanon der vorislamischen Zeit

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r5.claim: The text does not explicitly criticize particular pre-Islamic Arab virtues.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r5.anchor: doch kritisiert der Text nicht ausdrücklich bestimmte altarabische Tugenden.

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r14.claim: Al-khayr often means wealth, as in 2:180; wealth is called good because people want its worldly benefit and imagine it wholly good, a presumption condemned here.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r14.anchor: “Hayr” Kur’ân’ın إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا [el-Bakara 2/180] gibi birçok âyetlerinde mal mânasına

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r15.claim: One explanation of shadīd is miserly: the person loves wealth but refuses to spend it on God's due or public benefit.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r15.anchor: Yani mal ve serveti mutlaka hayır zannederek sevdiği için bahîldir, sıkıdır

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r16.claim: Another explanation makes him strong in acquiring and hoarding wealth but weak in paying its due and thanking God.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r16.anchor: Onu kazanmak, eline geçirip toplamak hususunda kavîdir, harîstir

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r17.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r17.claim: The Kashshaf offers a reading Elmalılı calls clearer: the person is constricted and displeased by good works requiring money or bodily effort.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r17.anchor: Keşşâf üçüncü bir vecih daha söylemiştir ki daha açık görünür

ELMALILI:100:5-11#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:5-11#2/r1.claim: The passage urges willingly spending wealth for good works and preparing available force for God's cause, rather than hoarding; it invokes Anfal 8:60.
ELMALILI:100:5-11#2/r1.anchor: Allah yolunda kuvvet hazırlamak için seve seve mal sarfederek hayra çalışmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r8.speaker: Râgıb el-İsfahânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r8.claim: Hayr can mean things people generally desire, such as reason, justice, virtue, or something beneficial.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r8.anchor: Râgıb el-İsfahânî, “akıl, adalet, fazilet, faydalı nesne gibi genellikle insanların rağbet ettiği şey” şeklinde tarif etmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r9.claim: Ancient Arabs often used hayr for wealth and especially horses; here it means abundant wealth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r9.anchor: Eski Araplar’da kelime sıklıkla “mal” ve özellikle “at” anlamında kullanılmaktaydı. Burada “çok mal, servet” mânasında kullanıldığı anlaşılmaktadır

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r9.claim: Khayr means wealth; shadid means miserly, as miserly people are called severe or hardened.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r10.claim: An alternative reads shadid as strong: the person intensely loves wealth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r10.anchor: وقيل: معناه وإنه لحب الخير لقوي، أي شديد الحب للخير أي المال.

BAYDAWI-FULL:100:6-11/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:100:6-11/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:100:6-11/r3.claim: Al-khayr means wealth; being intense in love of it means either miserly or strongly attached to it.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r5.claim: Al-khayr here means wealth; humanity loves it intensely and hoards it, preferring its immediate visible benefit over the delayed, unseen benefit of serving God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r5.anchor: أي المال الذي لا يعد غيره لجهله خيرا

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb gives a pilgrimage reading: departure from ʿArafa, kindled fires, departure from Muzdalifa at dawn, the valley floor, and reaching Mina's Jamʿ.
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: الدفعة من عرفة {فالموريات قدحا} قال: النيران تجمع {فالمغيرات صبحا}

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r10.claim: 'He is a witness to that' refers to the human being.
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {وإنه على ذلك لشهيد

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r11.claim: 'Good' in 'he loves good intensely' means wealth.
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {وإنه على ذلك لشهيد} قال: الإنسان {وإنه لحب الخير} قال: المال

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r12.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r12.claim: Another gloss takes 'a witness to that' to mean God is witness.
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r12.anchor: عن مجاهد {وإنه على ذلك لشهيد} قال: الله عز وجل

BURSEVI:v10p384/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p384/r1.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p384/r1.claim: Al-Qāshānī says the human is ungrateful by being veiled from God by His favors, stopping at the favors instead of using them to reach Him.
BURSEVI:v10p384/r1.anchor: وقال القاشاني لكفور لربه باحتجابه بنعمه عنه ووقوفه معها وعدم استعماله لها فيما ينبغي ليتوصل بها إليه.

BURSEVI:v10p384/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p384/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p384/r2.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads ingratitude as claiming independent ownership of existence and divine attributes, misusing them, or hoarding them instead of sharing guidance.
BURSEVI:v10p384/r2.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : لكنود بنعمة الوجود والصفات والأسماء لادعائها لنفسه بالاستقلال والاستبداد أو لعاص باستعمالها في غير محالها أو لبخيل لاختصاصها لنفسه وعدم إيثارها على

BURSEVI:v10p384/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p384/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p384/r4.claim: Al-khayr means wealth and worldly pursuit, as in 2:180; calling even illicit wealth good follows customary usage, just as the Qurʾan calls battle harm because people use that convention.
BURSEVI:v10p384/r4.anchor: فإن قلت سمى الله الجنس المال خيرا وعسى أن يكون خبيثا وحراما قلت أنما سماه خيرا جريا على العادة

BURSEVI:v10p384/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p384/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p384/r5.claim: La-shadīd means energetic and capable in pursuing wealth but weak and negligent in worship and gratitude; it can also mean miserly because spending wealth weighs on him.
BURSEVI:v10p384/r5.anchor: لشديد} أي قوى مطيق مجد في طلبه وتحصيله متهالك عليه وهو لحب عبادة الله وشكر نعمته ضعيف متقاعس

BURSEVI:v10p384/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p384/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p384/r6.claim: Mentioning love of wealth after ingratitude hints that greed drives hypocrites: their outward profession of faith protects their property and earns them a share of the spoils.
BURSEVI:v10p384/r6.anchor: ولعل وصفه بهذا الوصف القبيح بعد وصفه بالكنود للإيماء إلى أن من جملة الأمور الداعية للمنافقين إلى

BURSEVI:v10p384/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p384/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p384/r7.claim: The Persian couplets advise giving away wealth to receive lasting return and benefit companions rather than leaving treasure for heirs to regret.
BURSEVI:v10p384/r7.anchor: دهند وبراي وارث منه كه داغ حسرت بردل

TUSTARI:100:8/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:100:8/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:100:8/r1.claim: The worldly loves of self, the world, and desire are called good by convention among their adherents.
TUSTARI:100:8/r1.anchor: قال: الخير المراد هاهنا ثلاث: حب النفس وحب الدنيا وحب الهوى، فسماها خيرا لتعارف أهلها،

TUSTARI:100:8/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:100:8/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:100:8/r2.claim: True good is independence from creation, neediness toward God, and fulfilling His command.
TUSTARI:100:8/r2.anchor: وإنما الخير ثلاث: الاستغناء عن الخلق والافتقار إلى الله عز وجل وأداء الأمر.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r5.claim: Shadid means miserly; Abu Dhuʾayb's elegy witnesses this sense, and al-jawl means soil or earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r5.anchor: والشديد : البخيل . قال أبو ذؤيب راثيا :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r6.claim: Al-shadid can also mean a miserly, grasping person, as in the phrase by al-Tarafa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r6.anchor: كما يقال للبخيل المتشدد أيضا قال طرفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r7.claim: The lām in li-hubb al-khayr is causal and khayr means wealth; the human's innate miserliness springs from wanting more of it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r7.anchor: واللام في { لحب الخير } لام التعليل ، والخير : المال قال تعالى :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r8.claim: Fronting love of wealth highlights the striking motive and preserves the rhyme, despite lām al-ibtida's normal precedence, because the phrase is governed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p504/r8.anchor: وتقديم { لحب الخير } على متعلقه للاهتمام بغرابة هذا المتعلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p505/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p505/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p505/r1.claim: Love of money prompts withholding charity; Arabs disparaged miserliness yet hoarded from the weak and orphans while spending ostentatiously on drinking and gambling.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p505/r1.anchor: وكان العرب يعيرون بالبخل وهم مع ذلك يبخلون في الجاهلية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467#2/r2.claim: Good means wealth; the verse may mean intense love of money or greed and miserliness caused by that love, and Ibn Kathir accepts both readings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما: أن المعنى: وإنه لشديد المحبة للمال. والثاني: وإنه لحريص بخيل؛ من محبة المال.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p536#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p536#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p536#6/r1.claim: He is intensely attached to wealth, meaning miserly about it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p536#6/r1.anchor: {وإنه لحب الخير لشديد} أي [وإنه] لحب المال لبخيل (3)

KASHSHAF:100:7/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:7/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:100:7/r3.claim: ‘Al-khayr’ means wealth, as in the verse concerning what someone leaves behind.
KASHSHAF:100:7/r3.anchor: { الخير } المال ،   من قوله تعالى : { إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا }

KASHSHAF:100:8/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:8/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:100:8/r1.claim: ‘Shadīd’ can mean miserly and withholding; loving wealth while finding spending burdensome makes him stingy.
KASHSHAF:100:8/r1.anchor: والشديد : البخيل الممسك .   يقال : فلان شديد ومتشدّد .

KASHSHAF:100:8/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:8/r2.speaker: طرفة
KASHSHAF:100:8/r2.claim: Ṭarafah’s verse uses ‘al-mutashaddid’ for the miserly man whose valuable property death selects.
KASHSHAF:100:8/r2.anchor: قال طرفة : أَرَى الْمَوْتَ يَعْتَامُ الْكِرَامَ وَيَصْطَفِي ***

KASHSHAF:100:8/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:8/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:100:8/r3.claim: Alternatively, he is strong in loving wealth, preferring worldly life and pursuing it, but weak and sluggish in worshipping God and thanking Him.
KASHSHAF:100:8/r3.anchor: أو أراد بالشديد : القوي ،   وإنه لحب المال وإيثار الدنيا وطلبها قوي مطيق

KASHSHAF:100:8/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:8/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:100:8/r4.claim: Alternatively, he is constricted and closed in his love of good things, rather than open and expansive.
KASHSHAF:100:8/r4.anchor: أو أراد : أنه لحب الخيرات غير هش منبسط ،   ولكنه شديد منقبض .

MUQATIL:100:7-11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:100:7-11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:100:7-11/r2.claim: Good means wealth, and the human being loves wealth intensely.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#8/r1.claim: One explanation says the human is miserly because of his love of wealth; another says he is intensely attached to wealth but weak in worship of God.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#8/r1.anchor: لأجل حب المال لبخيل ممسك أو أنه لحب المال لقوى وهو لحب عبادة الله ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r1.claim: The pronoun refers without disagreement to the human; al-khayr means wealth, as in 2:180, and shadid means strong in loving wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r1.anchor:
وإنه } أي الإنسان من غير خلاف. { لحب الخير } أي المال ومنه قوله تعالى:
إن ترك خيرا

QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r2.claim: Another gloss takes shadid as miserly; Arabic calls a miser shadid or mutashaddid, as in Tarafa's verse, and fahish also means miser, as in 2:268.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r2.anchor:
وقيل: «لشديد» لبخيل. ويقال للبخيل: شديد ومتشدد. قال طرفة:
أرى الموت يعتام الكرام

QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says God calls wealth good because people consider it good, though it can be evil or unlawful; the same naming follows common usage in describing jihad as harm in 3:174.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r3.anchor: ابن زيد: سمى الله المال خيرا وعسى أن يكون شرا وحراما ولكن الناس يعدونه خيرا

QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r4.claim: Al-Farra says the full sense is strong in love of wealth, with love omitted after shadid because it has already appeared and for verse endings, as in the windy-day phrasing of 14:18.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:8/r4.anchor: الفراء: نظم الآية أن يقال: وإنه لشديد الحب للخير فلما تقدم الحب قال: شديد، وحذف من آخره ذكر الحب

QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r1.claim: Without faith, a person loves himself intensely and therefore loves worldly wealth, power, and pleasures as he imagines them.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r1.anchor: فهو شديد الحب لنفسه ،  ومن ثم يحب الخير

QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r2.claim: Faith transforms his priorities, turning ingratitude into gratitude and selfishness and greed into generosity and mercy, and reveals values greater than worldly possessions.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r2.anchor: فيغير من تصوراته وقيمه وموازينه واهتماماته

QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r3.claim: Without faith, human ambition remains petty, earthbound, limited by lifespan and trapped in the self; connection to God and the Hereafter alone liberates it.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r3.anchor: ومهما كبرت أطماعه .  واشتد طموحه ،  وتعالت أهدافه

QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:8/r4.claim: Faith connects earthly life to an eternal world from God, the Everlasting Origin, and returning to God, the Everlasting End.

STUDYQURAN:100:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:8/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:100:8/r1.claim: Most commentators understand ‘good things’ as wealth; it may more broadly mean worldly things loved excessively at the expense of God and the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:100:8/r1.anchor: Most commentators equate good things with wealth

SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r1.claim: The lam with shadid may mark capacity, meaning a person is strong enough to love wealth; shadid li-shayʾ can mean capable of it.
SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r1.anchor: أنها المعدية. والمعنى: وإنه لقوي مطيق لحب الخير يقال: هو شديد لهذا الأمر، أي: مطيق له

SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r2.claim: Alternatively, the lam is causal: love of money makes the person miserly. Some give it the sense of ʿala, but the author sees no need; shadid and mutashaddid can mean miserly, as the verse shows.
SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r2.anchor: أنها للعلة، أي: وإنه لأجل حب المال لبخيل. وقيل: اللام بمعنى " على ". ولا حاجة إليه

SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r3.claim: Al-Farra says the intended order is شديد الحب للخير; love was moved forward, with the repeated word omitted at the end, also to preserve verse endings, as in ʿasif day.
SAMIN-DURR:100:8/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: " أصل نظم الآية أن يقال: وإنه لشديد الحب للخير، فلما قدم " الحب " قال:

TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r1.speaker: بعض البصريين
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r1.claim: Some Basran grammarians take “severe” to mean miserly because of love of wealth, citing Tarafa’s verse describing the avaricious miser.
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r1.anchor: ببيت طرفة بن العبد اليشكري: [البحر الطويل] أرى الموت يعتام النفوس ويصطفي … عقيلة مال الباخل المتشدد

TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the wording to mean that the person is strong in his love of wealth.
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: معناه: وإنه لحب الخير لقوي.

TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r3.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r3.claim: Some Kufan grammarians say the expected order is “strong in love of wealth”; love was advanced and then omitted from the end for concision and the verse endings.
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: كان موضع {لحب} [العاديات: 8] أن يكون بعد شديد، وأن يضاف شديد إليه

TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r4.claim: The Kufan grammarians compare the omitted final word to the wind in “a day made harsh by the wind,” with the preceding mention allowing its omission.
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r4.anchor: قال: ومثله في سورة إبراهيم: {كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف} [إبراهيم: 18] والعصوف لا يكون لليوم، إنما يكون للريح؛

TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says wealth is worldly life and cites “if he leaves wealth” as evidence; even unlawful property is called good because people regard it as good.
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وإنه لحب الخير لشديد} [العاديات: 8] قال: " الخير: الدنيا؛

TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd notes that people call fighting bad, although it is not bad with God, citing the believers’ return without harm.
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r6.anchor: وسمي القتال في سبيل الله سوءا، وقرأ قول الله: {فانقلبوا بنعمة من الله وفضل لم يمسسهم سوء} [آل عمران: 174] قال: لم يمسسهم قتال؛

TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r7.claim: The intended sequence is that the human is ungrateful, intensely loves wealth, and God witnesses this; the witness clause is fronted as an intervening parenthesis.
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r7.anchor: وتأويل الكلام: إن الإنسان لربه لكنود، وإنه لحب الخير لشديد، وإن الله على ذلك من أمره لشاهد. ولكن قوله: {وإنه على ذلك لشهيد} [العاديات: 7] قدم

TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r8.claim: Qatada says the witness clause belongs earlier in the syntax: God witnesses that the human intensely loves wealth.
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود وإنه على ذلك لشهيد} [العاديات: 7] قال: هذا في مقاديم الكلام، قال: يقول: إن الله لشهيد

THALABI:v10p271#2/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p271#2/r17.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p271#2/r17.claim: God calls wealth good because people call it good, though it may be impure or unlawful; likewise He calls battle a bad thing because people regard it as bad, as in 3:174.
THALABI:v10p271#2/r17.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: سمى الله المال خيرا وعسى أن يكون خبيثا وحراما ولكن الناس يعدونه خيرا

THALABI:v10p271#2/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p271#2/r18.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p271#2/r18.claim: Because of his love of wealth, the person is exceedingly miserly; shadīd and mutashaddid can both describe a miser.
THALABI:v10p271#2/r18.anchor: ومعنى الآية وإنه من أجل حب المال لشديد بخيل، ويقال للبخيل: شديد ومتشدد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r1.speaker: جميع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r1.claim: All commentators take “good” here to mean wealth; revelation elsewhere also calls wealth good, reflecting ordinary usage rather than its ultimate outcome.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r1.anchor: الخير: المال هاهنا في قول الجميع (¬2)، والله تعالى. سمى المال خيرا في مواضع من التنزيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd explains that people call the wounds and harms of war “bad” according to their convention, not because those harms are bad in the ultimate outcome.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r2.anchor: وهذا كما أنه سمي ما ينال المجاهد من الجراح وأذى الحرب (¬5) سوءا في قوله: {لم يمسسهم سوء} [آل عمران: 174] على ما يتعارفه الناس بينهم، لا على أنه سوء في العاقبة. ذكر ذلك ابن زيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Zajjaj gloss “severe” as miserly; the poet Tarafa uses “the miserly, ungenerous” as evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة، (والزجاج) (¬7): يقال للبخيل: شديد ومتشدد، وأنشد لطرفة:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r4.claim: The commentators’ meaning is that a person is miserly because of love of wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r4.anchor: المعنى: فإن (¬3) الإنسان من أجل حب المال لبخيل، (وهذا معنى قول المفسرين) (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba proposes inversion: the meaning is that love of wealth is strong, with “love” moved later and the pronoun earlier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r5.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: معناه: وإن حبه للخير شديد، فأخر الحب وقدم الهاء، ذكره في باب المقلوب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari rejects inversion as unnecessary: the ordinary wording is sound, and the lām in “love” means “because of.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r6.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: ولا يجوز أن يحمل هذا على القلب؛ لأنه لا ضرورة تحوج إلى ذلك، وهو صحيح المعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r7.claim: Al-Farra allows “strong in love of wealth,” with the second “love” understood from the first, like an omitted “wind” after “windy day.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p254/r7.anchor: قال الفراء: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: وانه لحب الخير لشديد الحب، فاكتفى بالحب الأول من الثاني

WAHIDI-QT:100:8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:100:8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:100:8/r1.claim: “Good” means wealth; the intense love of money makes the person miserly.
WAHIDI-QT:100:8/r1.anchor: { وإنه لحب الخير } لأجل حب المال { لشديد } لبخيل

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:8:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:8:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:8:anmerkung/r1.claim: The attachment to wealth reflects love of possessions and worldly life, with parallels in 89:20, 76:8, and 75:20.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:8:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zur Liebe zum Besitz und zum Diesseits allgemein s. frühmekkanisch 89:20 (wa-tuḥibbūna l-māla ḥubban ǧammān), 76:8

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:9-11:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:9-11:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:9-11:kommentar/r2.claim: The sequence from accusation of wrongdoing to eschatological consequences also appears in Q104 in another literary form and recalls the basic form of Old Testament doom prophecy.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:9-11:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die Sequenz aus einer Anklage menschlichen Fehlverhaltens (Q 100:6–8) und dem Aufweis der daraus folgenden eschatologischen Konsequenzen (Q 100:9–11) findet sich in anderer literarischer Gestalt auch in Q 104

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Riddling that creates rhetorical tension also structures oath sequences such as Q 100 and teaching questions at 90:12–16, 97:2–4, 101:1–11, and 104:5–9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: auf dem Einsatz von Änigmatisierung zur Erzeugung rhetorischer Spannung basieren aber auch Schwurserien wie zu Beginn von Q 100

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p391#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p391#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p391#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قال ﴿ لحب الخير ﴾ هو المال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r1.claim: Al-khayr means wealth in Qur'anic usage, sometimes abundant wealth; it is called good from people's perspective though wealth can become evil in the afterlife. The lām is causal: intense because of love of money.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r1.anchor: أى المال وورد بهذا المعنى فى القرآن هو المال وخصه بعضهم بالمال الكثير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r2.claim: Shadid can mean miser, either passively tightened against generosity or actively keeping his money bag shut; more likely it means powerful, intensively loving wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r2.anchor: وجوز غير واحد ان يراد بالشديد القوى ولعله الاظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads him as strong in seeking money and worldly life but weak and slack in worship and gratitude to God; al-Alusi finds making the lām causal in that reading unclear.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r3.anchor: وهو لحب عبادة الله تعالى وشكر نعمته سبحانه ضعيف متقاعس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r4.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r4.claim: Al-Farra' explains the phrase as intense love of wealth, with the second occurrence of love omitted, like omitting wind after 'a stormy day'; Qutrub offers an alternative parsing as strong in love of wealth, which al-Alusi critiques as strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء يجوز ان يكون المعنى وانه لحب الخير لشديد الحب يعنى انه يحب المال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's discussion also allows al-khayr to mean good deeds from God, with the human constricted and unresponsive toward them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218#3/r5.anchor: ويفهم من كلام الزمخشرى فى الكشاف جواز أن يراد به ماهو عنده تعالى من الطاعات

BINTSHATI:v1p112/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p112/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p112/r4.claim: Those exegetes then switch the pronoun to the human in the next verse, breaking the unity of the three verses; they also gloss khayr as money, citing the bequest verse.
BINTSHATI:v1p112/r4.anchor: فتمزقت بهذا الصنيع وحدة السياق في الآيات الثلاث

BINTSHATI:v1p113/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r1.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r1.claim: Al-Raghib restricts khayr meaning wealth to a large amount of money.
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r1.anchor: لا يقال للمال خير حتى يكون كثيراً

BINTSHATI:v1p113/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r2.claim: Other Qur'anic contexts may support wealth as khayr, and the word once refers to horses in David's speech.
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r2.anchor: وجاء الخير مرة واحدة للخيل في آية (ص 32) على لسان داود:

BINTSHATI:v1p113/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r3.claim: Most Qur'anic uses of khayr mean better or best, about 125 occurrences, often with a comparative construction.
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r3.anchor: على أن لفظ الخير، أكثر ما يستعمل في القرآن بمعنى الأفضل

BINTSHATI:v1p113/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r4.claim: Khayr also explicitly contrasts with evil in several passages.
BINTSHATI:v1p113/r4.anchor: كما يأتي في القرآن، نقضاً للشر صراحة في مثل آيات

BINTSHATI:v1p114/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r1.claim: Khayr can also contrast with harm and misfortune, as in the cited passages.

BINTSHATI:v1p114/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r2.claim: Arabic permits khayr to mean wealth, horses, the opposite of evil, or goodness and virtue.
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r2.anchor: واللغة تحتمل أن يكون الخير للمال، والخيل، وضد الشر، والخيار والفضيلة

BINTSHATI:v1p114/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r3.claim: The context favors material wealth: an ungrateful person who testifies to his own ingratitude would intensely love money, not virtue.
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r3.anchor: غير أنسياق آية (العاديات) يرجح أن الخير فيها هو الخير المادي من مال أو شبهه

BINTSHATI:v1p114/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r4.claim: Shadd originally means a strong knot or binding, physically and metaphorically, as the cited verses show.
BINTSHATI:v1p114/r4.anchor: والأصل في الشد: قوة العقد والوثاق والإحكام، مادياً كما في آية

BINTSHATI:v1p115/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r1.claim: The Qur'an uses the phrase reaching one's full maturity and strength for growing into adulthood in several passages.
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r1.anchor: كما يعبر القرآن، عمن بلوغ الرشد والقوة بصيغة: بلغ أو يبلغ أشده

BINTSHATI:v1p115/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r2.claim: Shadid appears about forty times with punishment, divine might, seizure, or afterlife retribution, usually as warning and rebuke.
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r2.anchor: فجاءت في القرآن، في نحو أربعين موضعاً، مضافة إلى عذاب الله، وبطشه، وأخذه، وعقابه

BINTSHATI:v1p115/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r3.claim: Exceptional uses describe iron, Lot's wished-for strong support, Solomon's threatened punishment, and strong fighting forces.

BINTSHATI:v1p115/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r4.claim: The comparative ashad usually describes severity or force; its sole use for love is believers' greater love for God in 2:165.
BINTSHATI:v1p115/r4.anchor: وجاءت مرة واحدة مميزة بالحب في آية البقرة 165

BINTSHATI:v1p116/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p116/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p116/r1.claim: The Qur'an's usual threatening use of shidda adds menace to the interpreters' gloss of withholding and stinginess, in light of the preceding self-witness.
BINTSHATI:v1p116/r1.anchor: يضيف بلا شك، إلى ما اكتفى المفسرون به في آية العاديات، من معنى البخل والإمساك

DURR-FULL:v8p604/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p604/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p604/r2.claim: Qatada glossed الخير, “good,” here as wealth.
DURR-FULL:v8p604/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {وإنه لحب الخير} قال: هو المال

TAB:100:8/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:8/r1.speaker: author
TAB:100:8/r1.claim: The human being is intense in his love of wealth.
TAB:100:8/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره :  وإن الإنسان لحب المال لشديد

TAB:100:8/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:8/r2.speaker: بعض البصريين
TAB:100:8/r2.claim: Some Basran grammarians take “severe” to mean miserly: because of love of wealth, the person is stingy.
TAB:100:8/r2.anchor: فقال بعض البصريين :  معنى ذلك :  وإنه من أجل حب الخير لشديد :  أي لبخيل

TAB:100:8/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:8/r3.speaker: author
TAB:100:8/r3.claim: The Basrans cite Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd's description of a miser as al-mutashaddid to support “severe” meaning stingy.
TAB:100:8/r3.anchor: واستشهدوا لقوله ذلك ببيت طرفة بن العبد اليشكري :  أرى الموت يعتام النفوس ويصطفي *** عقيلة مال الباخل المتشدد

TAB:100:8/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:8/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB:100:8/r4.claim: Other grammarians understand the phrase as saying that the person is strong in his love of wealth.
TAB:100:8/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون :  معناه :  وإنه لحب الخير لقوي

TAB:100:8/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:8/r5.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB:100:8/r5.claim: A Kufan grammarian says the expected order is “severe in love of wealth”; fronting “love” licenses its omission after “severe,” also keeping the verse endings aligned, as in 14:18.
TAB:100:8/r5.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة :  كان موضع ( لحب ) أن يكون بعد شديد ،   وأن يضاف شديد إليه

TAB:100:8/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:8/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:100:8/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says khayr means worldly wealth, citing 2:180; people call wealth good even when it may be illicit or vile, and he notes that people call fighting “evil” although it is not evil with God.
TAB:100:8/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  {  وإنه لحب الخير لشديد } قال :  الخير :  الدنيا ،   وقرأ :  {  إن ترك خيرا الوصية }

TAB:100:8/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:8/r7.speaker: author
TAB:100:8/r7.claim: The clause that God witnesses this is semantically delayed: it interrupts the statement that the human is ungrateful and loves wealth.
TAB:100:8/r7.anchor: وتأويل الكلام :  إن الإنسان لربه لكنود ، وإنه لحب الخير لشديد ، وإن الله على ذلك من أمره لشاهد

TAB:100:8/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:8/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB:100:8/r8.claim: Qatada says the witness clause comes earlier in the wording but means that God witnesses the human's intense love of wealth.
TAB:100:8/r8.anchor: عن قتادة {  إن الإنسان لربه لكنود وإنه على ذلك لشهيد } قال :  هذا في مقاديم الكلام

BAQILLANI:v1p96/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r1.claim: Bāqillānī presents the verses as Qur’anic examples of tarsīʿ combined with tajnīs, alongside other balanced endings and phrases.
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r1.anchor: ومن ذلك الترصيع مع التجنيس كقول ابن المعتز

BURHAN:v4p340/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p340/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p340/r1.claim: The lām in ‘he is intense in love of wealth’ is causal, equivalent to ‘because of’ (من أجل).
BURHAN:v4p340/r1.anchor: وللتعليل وهي التي يصلح موضعها من أجل

BURHAN:v3p448/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p448/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p448/r8.claim: A close-letter paronomasia changes one letter between its paired words; the author groups several Qur'anic pairs under this form.
BURHAN:v3p448/r8.anchor: وإما لاحق بأن يختلف أحد الحرفين كقوله ﴿ وإنه على ذلك لشهيد وإنه لحب الخير لشديد ﴾

BURHAN:v4p41/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p41/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p41/r8.claim: The lām in liḥubb al-khayr is causal and means 'because of his love.'
BURHAN:v4p41/r8.anchor: واللام للتعليل بمعنى من أجل كقوله تعالى

BURHAN:v3p290/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p290/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v3p290/r7.claim: Some classify the phrase as inversion, understanding it to mean that the person's love of wealth is intense.

BURHAN:v3p290/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p290/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p290/r8.claim: An alternative denies inversion: the intended meaning is that love of wealth makes him stingy, with شديد meaning stingy.
BURHAN:v3p290/r8.anchor: وقيل ليس منه لأن المقصود منه أنه لحب المال لبخيل والشدة البخل

BURHAN:v3p281/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p281/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p281/r9.claim: The reordered phrase means that he is intense in his love of wealth.
BURHAN:v3p281/r9.anchor: ﴿ وإنه لحب الخير لشديد ﴾ 2 أي لشديد لحب الخير

ITQAN:v3p232#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r3.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isba' identifies a rare pronoun shift: the passage starts by mentioning two subjects, turns from the human to report about his Lord, then returns to the human, a “shift of pronouns.”
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن أبي الاصبع جاء في القرآن من الالتفات قسم غريب جدا لم أظفر في الشعر بمثاله

ITQAN:v2p497/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p497/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p497/r5.claim: The lām may be causative: the verse means that because of his love of wealth, a person is intensely miserly.
ITQAN:v2p497/r5.anchor: والتعليل نحو ﴿ وإنه لحب الخير لشديد ﴾ أي وإنه من أجل حب المال لبخيل

ITQAN:v3p245/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p245/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p245/r2.claim: The jinas al-lahiq type differs by a non-neighboring letter; examples include hamaza/lamaza, shahid/shadid, tafraḥun/tamraḥun, and amr/al-amn.
ITQAN:v3p245/r2.anchor: ومنها اللاحق بأن يختلفا بحرف غير مقارب فيه كذلك كقوله ﴿ ويل لكل همزة لمزة ﴾

KHATTABI:v1p37/r6.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p37/r6.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p37/r6.claim: An objection calls the construction awkward, since speakers would say that they are intense in their love of someone or wealth.
KHATTABI:v1p37/r6.anchor: وأنت لا تسمع فصيحا يقول: أنا لحب زيد شديد

KHATTABI:v1p44/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p44/r5.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p44/r5.claim: Shadīd here means miserly; Arabic also calls a miser shadīd or mutashaddid, as illustrated by Ṭarafa’s verse.
KHATTABI:v1p44/r5.anchor: وأن الشديد معناه هاهنا البخيل , ويقال: رجل شديد ومتشدد أي بخيل

KHATTABI:v1p44/r6.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p44/r6.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p44/r6.claim: The lām means ‘because of love of wealth’; khayr denotes wealth, and the phrase describes miserliness driven by that love.
KHATTABI:v1p44/r6.anchor: واللام في قوله: {لحب الخير} بمعنى لأجل حب الخير وهو المال

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p287/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p287/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p287/r4.claim: The fifteenth sense is worldly wealth or worldly goods.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p287/r4.anchor: والخامس عشر : الدنيا . ومنه قوله تعالى في العاديات

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r3.claim: Here الخير means wealth and شديد means miserly; Arabic also says رجل شديد or متشدد of a miser.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r3.anchor: وأراد بقوله: وإنه لحب الخير لشديد (8) [العاديات: 8]

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r1.claim: The pronoun in wa-innahu refers to the human.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r1.anchor: { وإنه } : أي وإن الإنسان ،   { لحب الخير }

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r3.claim: On the direct reading, the human is intense in love of wealth.

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r4.claim: An alternative gloss takes the phrase to mean miserly and controlling with wealth; a miser is called severe or intensely restrictive.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r4.anchor: وقيل : لبخيل بالمال ضابط له ،   ويقال للبخيل : شديد ومتشدد

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r5.claim: Ṭarafa’s verse uses al-mutashaddid of a miser whose wealth is coveted by death.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r5.anchor: وقال طرفة : أرى الموت يعتام الكرام ويصطفي *** عقيلة مال الفاحش المتشدد

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r6.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r6.claim: Qatāda says al-khayr wherever it occurs in the Qurʾān means wealth.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة : الخير من حيث وقع في القرآن هو المال

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows worldly good—wealth, health, and favor from rulers—because disbelievers and the ignorant know no other good; love of the afterlife’s good is praiseworthy.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية : ويحتمل أن يراد هذا الخير الدنيوي من مال وصحة وجاءه عند الملوك ونحوه ،   لأن الكفار والجهال لا يعرفون غير ذلك

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r8.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ paraphrases the syntax as شديد الحب للخير: love is placed first and the repeated word love is omitted at the end.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r8.anchor: وقال الفراء : نظم الآية أن يقال : وإنه لشديد الحب للخير . فلما تقدم الحب قال لشديد ،   وحذف من آخره ذكر الحب لأنه قد جرى ذكره

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r9.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the omission also suits the verse endings, comparing يوم عاصف, where the day is understood as windy.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r9.anchor: ولرءوس الآي كقوله تعالى : { في يوم عاصف } والعصوف : للريح لا للأيام

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r10.claim: Another analysis says the construction is not an ellipsis: the lām in li-ḥubb is causal, meaning that love of money makes him miserly.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r10.anchor: وقال غيره ما معناه : لأنه ليس أصله ذلك التركيب ،   بل اللام في { لحب } لام العلة ،   أي وإنه لأجل حب المال لبخيل

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r11.claim: Alternatively, he is strong and capable in loving and preferring wealth, yet weak and slack in worshipping God and thanking His blessings.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r11.anchor: أو وإنه لحب المال وإيثاره قوي مطيق ،   وهو لحب عبادة الله وشكر نعمه ضعيف متقاعس

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r12.claim: Calling someone strong for an affair means that he can manage it and has mastery of it.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r12.anchor: تقول : هو شديد لهذا الأمر وقوي له إذا كان مطيقا له ضابطا

ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that the person is not open-handed toward good things but remains tight-fisted and withdrawn.
ABUHAYYAN:100:8/r13.anchor: قال الزمخشري : أو أراد : وإنه لحب الخيرات غير هش منبسط ،   ولكنه شديد منقبض

ALUSI:100:8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:8/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī explains al-khayr here as wealth, a frequent Qur'anic usage.
ALUSI:100:8/r1.anchor: أي المال وورد بهذا المعنى في القرآن كثيراً

ALUSI:100:8/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI:100:8/r2.claim: Ikrima claims that al-khayr means wealth wherever it occurs in the Qur'an.
ALUSI:100:8/r2.anchor: حتى زعم عكرمة أن الخير حيث وقع في القرآن هو المال

ALUSI:100:8/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:8/r3.claim: Some restrict al-khayr to abundant wealth and read it that way in the bequest verse.
ALUSI:100:8/r3.anchor: وخصه بعضهم بالمال الكثير وفسر به في قوله تعالى

ALUSI:100:8/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:8/r4.claim: Calling wealth good reflects people's judgment; some wealth is evil on Judgment Day.
ALUSI:100:8/r4.anchor: وإطلاق كونه خيراً باعتبار ما يراه الناس وإلا فمنه ما هو شر يوم القيامة

ALUSI:100:8/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:8/r5.claim: The lām in li-ḥubb is causal: he is intensely miserly because of love of wealth.
ALUSI:100:8/r5.anchor: واللام للتعليل أي أنه لأجل حب المال

ALUSI:100:8/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:8/r6.claim: Shadīd means miserly; Arabic also calls a miser mutashaddid, as in a line by Ṭarafa.
ALUSI:100:8/r6.anchor: أي لبخيل كما قيل وكما يقال للبخيل شديد يقال له متشدد كما في قول طرفة

ALUSI:100:8/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:8/r7.claim: Shadīd may be passive, as though the miser is held back from generosity, or active, as though he ties his purse shut.
ALUSI:100:8/r7.anchor: فيه يجوز أن يكون بمعنى مفعول كأن البخيل شد عن الافضال ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى فاعل

ALUSI:100:8/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:8/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers shadīd as strong and the lām as in: intensely strong in loving wealth.
ALUSI:100:8/r8.anchor: ولعله الأظهر وكان اللام عليه بمعنى في أي وأنه لقوي مبالغ في حب المال

ALUSI:100:8/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:100:8/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says he is capable and strong in loving wealth and pursuing this world, but weak and sluggish in worship and gratitude.
ALUSI:100:8/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري المعنى وأنه لحب المال وإيثار الدنيا وطلبها قوي مطيق

ALUSI:100:8/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:8/r10.claim: Al-Nīsābūrī treats the lām causally in al-Zamakhsharī's reading, but al-Ālūsī says that parsing is not apparent.
ALUSI:100:8/r10.anchor: وجعل النيسابوري اللام على هذا التعليل وليس بظاهر فتأمل

ALUSI:100:8/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r11.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:100:8/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the phrase as intense love: he loves wealth and loves being its lover, with the second love omitted after the first.
ALUSI:100:8/r11.anchor: وقال الفراء يجوز أن يكون المعنى وأنه لحب الخير لشديد الحب يعني أنه يحب المال ويحب كونه محباً له

ALUSI:100:8/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r12.speaker: قطرب
ALUSI:100:8/r12.claim: Quṭrub construes shadīd li-ḥubb as severe because of love, analogizing it to a person who often strikes Zayd.
ALUSI:100:8/r12.anchor: وقال قطرب أي أنه شديد لحب الخير كقولك أنه لزيد ضروب في أنه ضروب لزيد

ALUSI:100:8/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:8/r13.claim: A proposed analysis makes shadīd an adjective linked to its raised verbal noun, then shifts and fronts the construction; al-Ālūsī objects that a predicate complement cannot precede it.
ALUSI:100:8/r13.anchor: وكونه مجروراً في مثل ذلك لا يجدي نفعاً إذ ليس هو فيه نحو زيد بك فرح

ALUSI:100:8/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:8/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:100:8/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's Kashshāf also allows al-khayr to mean good deeds: love of them leaves him strict and unexpansive.
ALUSI:100:8/r14.anchor: ويفهم من كلام الزمخشري في «الكشاف » جواز أن يراد به ما هو عنده تعالى

BAGHAWI:100:8/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:100:8/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:100:8/r1.claim: The human meant is the human being, and “good” here means wealth.
BAGHAWI:100:8/r1.anchor: وإنه } يعني الإنسان ، { لحب الخير } أي لحب المال

BAGHAWI:100:8/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:100:8/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:100:8/r2.claim: He is intensely attached to wealth and therefore miserly; Arabs call a miser shadīd or mutashaddid.
BAGHAWI:100:8/r2.anchor: لشديد } أي : لبخيل ، أي إنه من أجل حب المال لبخيل . يقال للبخيل : شديد ومتشدد

BAGHAWI:100:8/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:100:8/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:100:8/r3.claim: An alternative says he is strong in his love of wealth, meaning intensely attached to money.
BAGHAWI:100:8/r3.anchor: وقيل : معناه وإنه بحب الخير لقوي ، أي شديد ، أي : المال

BAYDAWI:100:8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:100:8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:100:8/r1.claim: Al-khayr here means wealth, as in the verse saying ‘if he leaves wealth’ (2:180).
BAYDAWI:100:8/r1.anchor: المال من قوله سبحانه وتعالى { إن ترك خيرا } أي مالا

BAYDAWI:100:8/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:100:8/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:100:8/r2.claim: Shadīd means stingy, or intensely attached to wealth.
BAYDAWI:100:8/r2.anchor: { لشديد } لبخيل ، أو لقوي مبالغ فيه

BIQAI:100:8/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:8/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:8/r1.claim: It is astonishing that a person denies the benefactor's kindness while bearing witness against himself; the verse identifies what drives that ingratitude.
BIQAI:100:8/r1.anchor: ولما كان من العجائب أن يكفر أحد إحسان المنعم ، وهو شاهد على نفسه ، ذكر الحامل له على ذلك حتى هان عليه

BIQAI:100:8/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:8/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:8/r2.claim: The pronoun refers to the human, despite his self-witness to ingratitude that merits the loss of blessings.
BIQAI:100:8/r2.anchor: أي الإنسان من حيث هو مع شهادته على نفسه بالكفر الذي يقتضي سلب النعم

BIQAI:100:8/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:8/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:8/r3.claim: The lām means “because of”; al-khayr means wealth, which the ignorant person counts as the only good.
BIQAI:100:8/r3.anchor: أي لأجل حب { الخير } أي المال الذي لا يعد غيره لجهله خيراً

BIQAI:100:8/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:8/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:8/r4.claim: Shadīd can mean miserly, keeping wealth tightly, or intensely powerful in his love of it.
BIQAI:100:8/r4.anchor: أي بخيل بالمال ، ضابط له ، ممسك عليه ، أو بليغ القوة في حبه

BIQAI:100:8/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:8/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:8/r5.claim: Wealth benefits in the present world, so people cling to what is immediate and tangible even though it distracts them from serving God; the unseen afterlife is neglected.
BIQAI:100:8/r5.anchor: لأن منفعته في الدنيا ، وهو متقيد بالعاجل الحاضر المحسوس ، مع علمه بأن أقل ما فيه أنه يشغله عن حسن الخدمة لربه ، وهو معرض عن الدين

BIQAI:100:8/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:8/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:8/r6.claim: The person is vigorous in loving wealth but weak and sluggish in worship, although love of good should lead to gratitude that brings increase.
BIQAI:100:8/r6.anchor: فهو لحب عبادة الله ضعيف متقاعس ، وكان حبه للخير يقتضي عنه الشكر الذي يتقاضى الزيادة

BIQAI:100:8/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:8/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:8/r7.claim: The preceding shadīd does not govern the following love phrase across the lām; it instead points to an omitted governed element.
BIQAI:100:8/r7.anchor: ولا يتخيل أن شديداً عامل في الحب ؛ لأن ما بعد اللام لا يعمل فيما قبلها ، وإنما ذلك المتقدم دليل على المعمول المحذوف

DURR:100:8/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:100:8/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR:100:8/r1.anchor: عن قتادة { وإنه لحب الخير } قال : هو المال .

IBNASHUR:100:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:8/r1.claim: The lām in li-ḥubb is causal, and al-khayr means wealth, as in the Qurʾānic phrase in taraka khayran.
IBNASHUR:100:8/r1.anchor: واللام في { لحب الخير } لام التعليل

IBNASHUR:100:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:8/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:8/r2.claim: Humans become intensely miserly because they love wealth and want to increase it; the verse recalls the warning that whoever is protected from the soul's stinginess succeeds.
IBNASHUR:100:8/r2.anchor: والمعنى :  إن في خلق الإنسان الشح لأجل حبه المال ،  أي الازدياد منه

IBNASHUR:100:8/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:8/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:8/r3.claim: The causal phrase is fronted to emphasize the surprising object of intense attachment and to preserve the verse's cadence; a genitive phrase may precede the predicate with its lām, as in verse 6.
IBNASHUR:100:8/r3.anchor: وتقديم { لحب الخير } على متعلقه للاهتمام بغرابة هذا المتعلق ولمراعاة الفاصلة ،  وتقديمه على عامله المقترن بلام الابتداء

IBNASHUR:100:8/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:8/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:8/r4.claim: Love of wealth drives people to withhold good. Arabs mocked miserliness yet denied support to the poor and weak, consumed orphans' estates, and lavishly spent for reputation, at drinking gatherings, and in gambling, as Sūrat al-Fajr describes.
IBNASHUR:100:8/r4.anchor: وحب المال يبعث على منع المعروف ،  وكان العرب يعيرون بالبخل وهم مع ذلك يبخلون في الجاهلية بمواساة الفقراء والضعفاء ويأكلون أموال اليتامى

IBNATIYYA:100:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r1.claim: The pronoun in wa-innahu refers only to the human being.
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r1.anchor: والضمير في قوله تعالى : { وإنه لحب الخير } عائد على { الإنسان } لا غير

IBNATIYYA:100:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r2.claim: Because of his love of wealth, he is intensely miserly and tightly holds onto it.
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r2.anchor: والمعنى من أجل حب الخير إنه { لشديد } ، أي بخيل بالمال ضابط له

IBNATIYYA:100:8/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r3.claim: Tarafa's verse calls the wealthy miser al-mutashaddid, the one who tightly hoards his wealth.
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r3.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر [ طرفة بن العبد ] : [ الطويل ] أرى الموت يعتام الكرام ويصطفي

IBNATIYYA:100:8/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r4.claim: In Qur'anic usage, khayr means wealth.
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r4.anchor: و { الخير } المال على عرف ذلك في كتاب الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:100:8/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r5.claim: Ikrima says khayr means wealth wherever it occurs in the Quran.
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r5.anchor: قال عكرمة : { الخير } حيث وقع في القرآن فهو المال

IBNATIYYA:100:8/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r6.claim: Khayr here may mean worldly advantages such as wealth, health, and standing with rulers, since disbelievers and ignorant people know no other good.
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد هنا الخير الدنياوي من مال وصحة وجاه عند الملوك ونحوه

IBNATIYYA:100:8/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r7.claim: By contrast, one who loves the good of the afterlife is praised and may hope for success.
IBNATIYYA:100:8/r7.anchor: فأما المحب في خير الآخرة فممدوح له مرجو له الفوز

IBNKATHIR:100:8/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:100:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:100:8/r1.claim: Here al-khayr means wealth; one view is that the person intensely loves wealth, which Ibn Kathir accepts along with the second view.
IBNKATHIR:100:8/r1.anchor: أي : وإنه لحب الخير - وهو : المال - لشديد

IBNKATHIR:100:8/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:100:8/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:100:8/r2.claim: The other valid view is that love of wealth makes the person greedy and miserly.
IBNKATHIR:100:8/r2.anchor: والثاني : وإنه لحريص بخيل ؛ من محبة المال

MAWARDI:100:8/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:8/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:100:8/r1.claim: The pronoun in the verse refers to the human being.
MAWARDI:100:8/r1.anchor: يعني الإنسان ، وفي الخير ها هنا وجهان :

MAWARDI:100:8/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:8/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI:100:8/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, and Qatada take al-khayr here to mean wealth.
MAWARDI:100:8/r2.anchor: أحدهما : المال ، قاله ابن عباس ، ومجاهد وقتادة .

MAWARDI:100:8/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:8/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI:100:8/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd takes al-khayr here to mean worldly life.

MAWARDI:100:8/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:8/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:100:8/r4.claim: A third possibility is that al-khayr means the person's chosen preference, so he strongly loves what he selects for himself.
MAWARDI:100:8/r4.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثاً : أن الخير ها هنا الاختيار ، ويكون معناه : وإنه لحب اختياره لنفسه لشديد .

MAWARDI:100:8/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:8/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:100:8/r5.claim: One explanation makes shadid describe the strength and increase of his love for wealth.
MAWARDI:100:8/r5.anchor: وفي قوله { لشديد } وجهان : أحدهما : لشديد الحب للخير ، وشدة الحب قوته وتزايده .

MAWARDI:100:8/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:8/r6.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:100:8/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says shadid means miserly: the person is stingy with wealth and withholds God's due.
MAWARDI:100:8/r6.anchor: الثاني : لشحيح بالمال يمنع حق الله منه ، قاله الحسن ، من قولهم : فلان شديد ، أي شحيح .

NASAFI:100:8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:100:8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:100:8/r1.claim: He may be fiercely attached to wealth, meaning miserly and withholding.
NASAFI:100:8/r1.anchor: وإنه لأجل حب المال لبخيل ممسك

NASAFI:100:8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:100:8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:100:8/r2.claim: Alternatively, he is powerful in his love of wealth but weak in his love of worshipping God.

QURTUBI:100:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:100:8/r1.claim: The pronoun in “indeed he” refers to the human, with no disagreement reported.
QURTUBI:100:8/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " وإنه " أي الإنسان من غير خلاف

QURTUBI:100:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:8/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:100:8/r2.claim: Al-khayr means wealth, as in the Qurʾānic phrase about leaving wealth in a will.
QURTUBI:100:8/r2.anchor: لحب الخير } أي المال ،   ومنه قوله تعالى : { إن ترك خيرا }

QURTUBI:100:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:8/r3.speaker: عدي
QURTUBI:100:8/r3.claim: ʿAdī’s poem uses al-khayr in the context of what souls seek, paired with love of life.
QURTUBI:100:8/r3.anchor: ماذا تُرَجِّي النفوسُ من طلب ال***خَيْرِ

QURTUBI:100:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:8/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:100:8/r4.claim: Shadīd means powerful in his love of wealth.
QURTUBI:100:8/r4.anchor: " لشديد " أي لقوي في حبه للمال

QURTUBI:100:8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:8/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:100:8/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes shadīd to mean miserly; a miser is called shadīd or mutashaddid, as in Ṭarafa’s verse about a miserly owner of choice wealth.
QURTUBI:100:8/r5.anchor: وقيل : " لشديد " لبخيل .   ويقال للبخيل : شديد ومتشدد

QURTUBI:100:8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:100:8/r6.claim: Al-fāḥisha can mean miserliness, as in 2:268.
QURTUBI:100:8/r6.anchor: والفاحش : البخيل أيضا .   ومنه قوله تعالى : { ويأمركم بالفحشاء }

QURTUBI:100:8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:8/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI:100:8/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says God calls wealth good because people regard it as good although it may be evil and unlawful; similarly, people call jihad harmful in 3:174.
QURTUBI:100:8/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد : سمى الله المال خيرا ،   وعسى أن يكون شرا وحراما

QURTUBI:100:8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:8/r8.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:100:8/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains an order shift from “strong in love of wealth”: love is omitted at the end because it was just mentioned and for the verse ending, like “a stormy day” with wind understood in 14:18.
QURTUBI:100:8/r8.anchor: قال الفراء : نظم الآية أن يقال : وإنه لشديد الحب للخير ،   فلما تقدم الحب قال : شديد

RAZI:100:8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:8/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:100:8/r1.claim: Al-khayr here means wealth, as in 2:180 and 70:21; people call money good, just as the Qur'an calls war wounds harm in 3:174.
RAZI:100:8/r1.anchor: الخير المال من قوله تعالى : { إن ترك خيرا } وقوله : { وإذا مسه الخير منوعا } وهذا لأن الناس يعدون المال فيما بينهم خيرا كما أنه تعالى سمى ما ينال المجاهد من الجراح وأذى الحرب سوءا

RAZI:100:8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:8/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:100:8/r2.claim: Here shadīd means miserly and withholding; Arabic also calls someone shadīda or mutashaddid.

RAZI:100:8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:8/r3.speaker: طرفة
RAZI:100:8/r3.claim: Ṭarafa's verse uses al-mutashaddid to describe a grasping rich miser, supporting شديد as withholding wealth.
RAZI:100:8/r3.anchor: قال طرفة : أرى الموت يعتام الكرام ويصطفي *** عقيلة مال الفاحش المتشدد

RAZI:100:8/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:8/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:100:8/r4.claim: One explanation says love of wealth makes a person miserly and tight-fisted.
RAZI:100:8/r4.anchor: ( أحدها ) : أنه لأجل حب المال لبخيل ممسك

RAZI:100:8/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:8/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:100:8/r5.claim: Another takes shadīd as strong and capable: people vigorously seek wealth and worldly life but are weak in worshipping God and thanking Him.
RAZI:100:8/r5.anchor: ( وثانيها ) : أن يكون المراد من الشديدة القرى ، ويكون المعنى وإنه لحب المال وإيثار الدنيا وطلبها قوي مطيق ، وهو لحب عبادة الله وشكر نعمه ضعيف

RAZI:100:8/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:8/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:100:8/r6.claim: A third view says his love of wealth is constricted rather than generous: he holds it tightly and does not give freely.
RAZI:100:8/r6.anchor: ( وثالثها ) : أراد إنه لحب الخيرات غير هني منبسط ولكنه شديد منقبض

RAZI:100:8/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:8/r7.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:100:8/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads شديد الحب, “intense in love of wealth,” with the second الحب omitted; he compares 14:18, where الريح is not repeated after عاصف.
RAZI:100:8/r7.anchor: قال الفراء : يجوز أن يكون المعنى وإنه لحب الخير لشديد الحب

RAZI:100:8/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:8/r8.speaker: قطرب
RAZI:100:8/r8.claim: Quṭrub likewise paraphrases the phrase as شديد حب الخير, like calling someone “much striking for Zayd.”
RAZI:100:8/r8.anchor: قال قطرب : أي إنه شديد حب الخير

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r14.claim: The human is a witness to his own hoards.

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r15.claim: Love of wealth makes the human miserly; shadid means stingy because of love of wealth.
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r15.anchor: أي : وإنه لبخيل لأجل حب المال

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r22.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r22.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r22.claim: The human-witness phrase may instead mean God witnesses the human's condition.
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r22.anchor: يحتمل : وإن الله على حاله لشهيد

MAJAZ:v2p307/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p307/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p307/r7.claim: The human is miserly because of love of wealth; shadid and mutashaddid are terms for a miser.

MAJAZ:v2p307/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p307/r8.speaker: طرفة
MAJAZ:v2p307/r8.claim: Ṭarafa's line uses mutashaddid for the miser whose wealth death selects.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p419/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p419/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p419/r2.claim: Khayr here means wealth; man hoards blessings as his own achievement, unlike the obedient horse that returns its spoils and accepts its master's feed, while boasting as in Qārūn's claim.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p419/r2.anchor: whatever favours man is blessed with by the Almighty are regarded by him to be the result of his own planning and skill

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p419/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p419/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p419/r3.claim: God, man's creator and benefactor, is truly worthy of love; believers prefer Him when self-interest conflicts, while the ungrateful cherish wealth more than their Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p419/r3.anchor: the believers are the most stern in their love for God

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r16.claim: The human is strongly attached to good, meaning wealth; shadīd means intense in love, though it may instead mean tightfisted and controlling of wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r16.anchor: وإنه: أي وإن الإنسان، لحب الخير: أي المال، لشديد: أي قوي في حبه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r17.speaker: طرفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r17.claim: Ṭarafa's line uses al-mutashaddid for a person who tightly hoards wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r17.anchor: وقال طرفة: أرى الموت يعتام الكرام ويصطفي ... عقيلة مال الفاحش المتشدد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r1.claim: Qatāda says that wherever khayr occurs in the Qur'an it means wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r1.anchor: وقال قتادة: الخير من حيث وقع في القرآن هو المال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows worldly goods such as wealth, health, and favor with rulers; ignorant unbelievers know no other good, whereas love of afterlife's good is praiseworthy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد هذا الخير الدنيوي من مال وصحة وجاءه عند الملوك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the syntax means intense love of wealth, with the final word for love omitted because it has already appeared and to preserve the verse ending.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r3.anchor: فلما تقدم الحب قال لشديد، وحذف من آخره ذكر الحب لأنه قد جرى ذكره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r4.claim: Another analysis treats the lām as causal: because of love of wealth the person is miserly or intensely attached to it, while weak in worship and gratitude.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r4.anchor: بل اللام في لحب لام العلة، أي وإنه لأجل حب المال لبخيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses shadīd as closed and constricted rather than openhanded toward goods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p530/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أو أراد: وإنه لحب الخيرات غير هش منبسط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r4.claim: The pronoun in the love-of-good clause refers to the human being; because of love for wealth he is intensely miserly and guards it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى من أجل حب الخير إنه لشديد، أي بخيل بالمال ضابط له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r5.claim: Ikrima says that wherever good appears in the Quran it means wealth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r5.anchor: قال عكرمة: الخير حيث وقع في القرآن فهو المال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r6.claim: Here good may mean worldly wealth, health, and status, which disbelievers and the ignorant value; loving the good of the Hereafter is praiseworthy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد هنا الخير الدنياوي من مال وصحة وجاه عند الملوك ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r7.speaker: طرفة بن العبد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r7.claim: Tarafa's verse about death selecting a miser's precious wealth illustrates the meaning of a person who hoards it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r7.anchor: أرى الموت يعتام الكرام ويصطفي ... عقيلة مال الفاحش المتشدد

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, ʿIkrimah, and Qatadah say the surah is Meccan; another view says it is Medinan and was revealed around a raid.
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.anchor: قيل: إنها مكية، عن الحسن، وعكرمة، وقتادة. وقيل: مدنية، وقالوا: نزلت عند جهاد وقع في سرية.

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for reciting the surah for every person who spent the night at Muzdalifah and witnessed Jamʿ.
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.anchor: من قرأ سورة (والعاديات) أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد من بات بالمزدلفة وشهد جمعا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r21.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r21.claim: Al-khayr means wealth, as in 2:180, and shadīd means miserly and withholding.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r21.anchor: { الخير } المال من قوله تعالى : { إن ترك خيرا } ( البقرة : 180 ) والشديد : البخيل الممسك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r22.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r22.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r22.claim: Shadīd is glossed as a miserly person who holds wealth back.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r22.anchor: والشديد : البخيل الممسك . يقال : فلان شديد ومتشدد .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r1.claim: Tarafah’s verse uses shadīd for a miserly person who hoards wealth.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r2.claim: Alternatively, shadīd means forceful: the person avidly pursues wealth and worldly life but is weak and slack in worship and gratitude.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r2.anchor: أو أراد بالشديد : القوي ، وأنه لحب المال وإيثار الدنيا وطلبها قوي مطيق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r3.claim: A further reading takes khayr as good deeds: the person loves them but remains constricted rather than generous and openhanded.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r3.anchor: أو أراد : أنه لحب الخيرات غير هش منبسط ، ولكنه منقبض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for reciting al-ʿĀdiyāt for every person who spent the night at Muzdalifah and witnessed Jamʿ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.anchor: ( 1335 ) ( من قرأ سورة والعاديات أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد من بات بالمزدلفة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.claim: The following Sūrat al-Qāriʿah is Meccan according to all the authorities mentioned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.anchor: سورة القارعة مكية في قولهم جميعا

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.claim: The Meccan surah has eleven verses and moves in rapid, forceful jumps before settling at its ending, like a runner reaching the finish.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.anchor: سورة العاديات مكية وآياتها إحدى عشرة يجري سياق هذه السورة في لمسات سريعة عنيفة مثيرة

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r3.claim: A second scene turns from the charge to human ingratitude, denial, selfishness, and intense miserliness.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r3.anchor: يليه مشهد في النفس من الكنود والجحود والأثرة والشح الشديد

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.claim: The rough, rumbling, cracking rhythm suits the noisy dust and forceful disclosure of graves and hearts, as well as the surah’s ingratitude and greed.
